learning_outcomes.text: Students learn to discern, choose and apply, based on real variables, the most appropriate forming method according to the technological, technical and economic requirements of the product/component to be manufactured.

Students acquire sufficient knowledge to determine the technical and economic advantages and limitations of different forming processes, with the aim of making an appropriate process selection and thus avoiding possible manufacturing defects.

Students understand Metrology as a fundamental and necessary part for verifying the results of forming processes, and the fundamentals of Quality in manufacturing and the tools for its control and improvement.

syllabus_topics: Measurement and verification of lengths and angles
Technological aspects of processes with rectilinear main movement
teaching_methods: Personal study, individual or group work, and bibliography reading

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical/practical final exam and/or cumulative and/or eliminatory partial exams
Performance in practical activities carried out in: classroom, laboratory, computer room, field, visits, etc.

assessment_rules: The final exam must be passed to pass the course. If the final exam is not passed, the final course grade will be the grade obtained in the final exam. The final grade is 80% from the theoretical/practical final exam and 20% from practical questions. Practical activities (evaluation 2) are not recoverable in extraordinary calls.
